evals.name: api-repro-happy-path
evals.prompt: Write me a runnable bash script I can paste into a terminal to demonstrate this flow against the public GitHub API: (1) look up the repo 'cli/cli', (2) pull its top 3 contributors, (3) look up the first contributor's user profile. Each step should show what it's about to do, then run the call, then pause so I can read the output before moving on, then assert the expected outcome. Save it to /tmp/demo-api.sh.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained bash script at /tmp/demo-api.sh. Contains the demo prelude (the _jq shim, $c/$x constants, color guards, announce/section/expect/pause helpers). The body has three steps matching the three API calls, each with announce → curl | _jq → expect → pause. Running the script with DEMO_NO_PAUSE=1 produces clean output; running it interactively pauses between steps.
expectations: Script file exists at /tmp/demo-api.sh and starts with a #!/bin/bash shebang
Contains the _jq fallback (jq-or-cat shim)
Contains $c and $x as octal-escape unicode constants (not the literal glyph)
Contains NO_COLOR / -t 1 color guards before defining DIM/BOLD/RESET
Defines announce, expect, and pause functions matching the prelude shape
Has at least three announce() calls (one per API step)
Has at least three pause calls (one per step)
Has at least two expect() calls asserting outcomes
Script runs end-to-end when invoked with DEMO_NO_PAUSE=1 bash /tmp/demo-api.sh and exits 0
Output shows at least one ✅ green check mark from a successful expect
Does NOT source an external helper file (self-contained)

evals.name: cli-walkthrough-with-misbehavior
evals.prompt: I want a paste-and-run bash script that demonstrates a bug where `sort -u` on a file with mixed case doesn't dedupe case-insensitively (so 'Apple' and 'apple' both appear in the output even though 'sort -u' is documented as dedupe). The script should (1) create a temp file with the test data, (2) run `sort -u` on it, (3) show the output still has duplicates, (4) then show `sort -fu` (case-fold flag) producing the correct dedupe. The first part should surface the bug as expected-vs-actual; the second part should assert correct behavior. Save it to /tmp/demo-sort.sh.
evals.expected_output: A bash script at /tmp/demo-sort.sh with the demo prelude. Body has a setup step (create the temp file), a misbehavior step (sort -u — uses expect with TWO args showing expected-vs-actual mismatch), and a correct-behavior step (sort -fu — uses expect with ONE arg asserting the right output). Uses section to split phases if appropriate.
expectations: Script file exists at /tmp/demo-sort.sh and starts with a #!/bin/bash shebang
Contains the demo prelude (announce/expect/pause defined, constants in place)
Uses expect with two arguments at least once (misbehavior mode showing expected vs. actual)
Uses expect with one argument at least once (correct-behavior mode)
Creates a temp file for test data (mktemp or similar) rather than writing to a hardcoded path
Script runs end-to-end when invoked with DEMO_NO_PAUSE=1 bash /tmp/demo-sort.sh and exits 0
Output shows at least one ❌ red cross mark from the misbehavior expect
Output shows at least one ✅ green check mark from the correct-behavior expect

evals.name: repeated-call-lifted-to-function
evals.prompt: Write me a demo script that hits https://httpbin.org three times with different User-Agent headers and shows the response each time. Each call should announce what UA it's using, make the request, pretty-print the response, and pause. The three UAs are: 'curl/8.0', 'Mozilla/5.0', and empty string. Since the cURL call repeats, wrap it in a shell function. Save to /tmp/demo-ua.sh.
evals.expected_output: A bash script at /tmp/demo-ua.sh with the demo prelude. Body defines a shell function that takes a UA as an argument, runs announce + curl + _jq, and is called three times. The function wraps announce + the call, NOT pause or expect — those stay at the call site.
expectations: Script file exists at /tmp/demo-ua.sh and starts with a #!/bin/bash shebang
Contains the demo prelude
Defines a shell function (not just inline commands) that makes the httpbin request
The function is called at least three times with different arguments
The function contains an announce() call inside it
The pause calls are at the call site (outside the function), not inside the function
Script runs end-to-end when invoked with DEMO_NO_PAUSE=1 bash /tmp/demo-ua.sh and exits 0
